content: 1. Administer streptomycin intramuscularly at a dose of 15 mg/kg every 12 hours for a minimum of 10 days, not exceeding 2 g/day. For patients older than 8 years, administer 20 mg/kg intramuscularly divided every 12 hours during 7–14 days of tetracycline or co-trimoxazole therapy, not exceeding 1 g/day. 2. Streptomycin enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of apnea. 3. Streptomycin and bacitracin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of bacitracin with other nephrotoxic drugs should also be avoided. 4. Streptomycin reduces the effects of the BCG live vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Streptomycin and bumetanide increase each other's toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased risks of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. 6. Streptomycin reduces the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration of the cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 7. Streptomycin reduces the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Antibacterial agents may decrease the efficacy of oral microbiota containing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 11.
